transcript.text: Dropped a cast iron pan on my ceramic hob and there's a crack right across the front left ring. It still heats up. Can I keep using it until I get a new one?

No, stop using it, ideally the whole hob and not just that ring. It might seem fine because it still heats, but a crack in a ceramic (glass-ceramic) hob is a real safety issue:

• Electric shock risk: The glass is the barrier between you and the live heating elements and wiring. A crack can let you, or a metal pan, come into contact with live parts.
• Liquid getting in: Boil-overs, spills, or even wiping it down can let water seep through the crack onto the electrics, causing shorts, shocks, or a fire risk.
• The crack can spread or shatter: Heating and cooling make the glass expand and contract, which stresses the crack. It can spread across the hob or, occasionally, break apart.
• Avoid nearby rings too: They're under the same sheet of glass, and heating them still puts thermal stress on the whole panel.

What to do now:
1. Switch it off at the isolator or wall switch (usually a large switch near the cooker, often labelled "cooker"). If there isn't one, turn off the circuit at the fuse box/consumer unit. This stops anyone using it by accident.
2. Don't clean it with a wet cloth while it's connected.
3. Don't try to seal it with glue or tape. It won't make it safe.

Next steps:
• Check your home insurance. Many policies cover accidental damage to hobs, sometimes even without specific accidental-damage cover, so it's worth a call.
• Ask about a replacement glass top. For some models you can replace just the glass, which may be cheaper than a new hob. Check the model number (usually on a sticker underneath or in the manual).
• Stopgaps in the meantime: A plug-in single or double hot plate, a portable induction hob (if your pans are induction-compatible, and cast iron is), a microwave, an air fryer, or the oven (if it's on a separate circuit from the hob) can tide you over.

Annoying, I know, but a cheap portable hob for a week or two is much better than risking a shock or fire.
